patch.value: Entity projections carry a collection key only when it is non-empty, so an absent key cannot be distinguished from an unprojected one and neither projection level is a superset of the other

An entity projection includes a collection key only when that collection is non-empty, so an absent key is ambiguous between "this collection is empty" and "this projection does not carry this collection". Nothing in the envelope resolves the ambiguity, and the two projection levels are not ordered by containment, so an agent cannot pick one and parse it stably.

Measured live on 2026-08-08 against three items. Default pm get --json on a freshly created item carries notes_count and tests_count but no comments key and no files key, while pm comments and pm files on the same item return one comment and two linked files. Adding --full adds comments and files and simultaneously removes notes_count and tests_count, so neither level is a superset of the other. Across items the --full key set varies with content rather than with schema: one item yields comments and files, another yields comments, learnings, notes, tests and test_runs, a third yields comments, docs, files, tests and test_runs. No fixed jq expression is valid across items, and a consumer that selects a collection key must first discover whether the key exists.

The realized agent failure, reproduced first-hand while filing pm-h75tjh in this pass: after pm files --add and pm comments --add both reported success, reading the item back through the default projection and selecting the collection lengths returned zero for both. That reads exactly like a silently failed write. Confirming the writes required two further command invocations, one per collection. This is the read-back half of the ergonomics complaint: the tool cannot be used to verify its own mutations without knowing, out of band, which projection carries which field.

A second instance of the same vocabulary problem sits on the same path. The write flag is --linked-file, the command noun is files, and the read key is files, so the name an agent writes with is not the name it reads back with.

Cost. Every verified mutation costs at least one extra invocation per collection touched, on a prescribed finish that already spans several invocations, and the extra call is pure overhead against a projection that could have carried the field.

Every entity projection level declares a stable key set: a collection the level carries is always present, empty collections render as empty, so an absent key means not carried and never means empty; The full projection is a proper superset of the default projection, proven by a test that diffs key sets over an item populated in every collection and an item populated in none; Every collection a mutation can write is readable from at least one documented entity projection, and the write flag, command noun and read key share one spelling; A negative control fails when a collection is added to the item model without a corresponding projection contract entry

value.text: Duplicate check before filing: searched projection omits collection, read back after write, absent key empty, get projection full superset, verify mutation landed. Nearest owners are all closed and cover different halves: pm-sb0tns (no common row contract across read surfaces, cited as discovered_from), pm-cyrfjq (mode-paired envelopes zero-fill the inactive collection, the inverse convention) and pm-v8gfi7 (provenance unreadable because the only projection carrying it drops other fields). Open sibling pm-1wujzi owns claim_state being absent from every list projection including full. None owns content-conditional key presence on entity projections or the non-containment of the two levels. Reproduced first-hand in this pass while verifying writes on pm-h75tjh.
